denomProfiles/montanist/tagline: Second-century prophetic movement awaiting the descent of the New Jerusalem in Phrygia.
denomProfiles/montanist/coreDoctrines/0: The Paraclete promised in John's Gospel speaks anew through the prophets Montanus, Priscilla and Maximilla.
denomProfiles/montanist/coreDoctrines/1: New prophecy completes rather than contradicts apostolic teaching; its oracles were written down and read.
denomProfiles/montanist/coreDoctrines/2: Imminent end: the heavenly Jerusalem would descend at Pepuza and Tymion in Phrygia.
denomProfiles/montanist/coreDoctrines/3: Stricter discipline than the mainstream church, including no remarriage after a spouse's death.
denomProfiles/montanist/coreDoctrines/4: Mainstream teaching on God and Christ; Tertullian's Trinitarian writing dates from his Montanist period.
denomProfiles/montanist/focuses/0: Ecstatic prophecy as a continuing gift of the Spirit.
denomProfiles/montanist/focuses/1: Moral rigour: extended fasts, celibacy and refusal to flee persecution.
denomProfiles/montanist/focuses/3: Prominent prophetic and clerical roles for women.
denomProfiles/montanist/practices/0: Ecstatic oracles spoken in the first person as the voice of the Spirit.
denomProfiles/montanist/practices/1: Extra fasts ('xerophagies' of dry food) beyond those kept by other churches.
denomProfiles/montanist/practices/2: Pilgrimage to Pepuza, later the seat of the movement's patriarch.
denomProfiles/montanist/practices/3: Women prophets, and according to Epiphanius women presbyters and bishops among some groups.
denomProfiles/montanist/influenced/0/tex: Reaction to new oracles pushed the mainstream church to emphasise a fixed apostolic Scripture.
denomProfiles/montanist/influenced/1/tex: The Carthaginian theologian adopted the New Prophecy around 207 and defended it in later works.
denomProfiles/montanist/influenced/2/tex: Some Pentecostal writers have claimed Montanists as forerunners, though there is no historical continuity.
denomProfiles/montanist/keyFigures/2/rol: Prophetess who predicted wars and the end after her death
denomProfiles/montanist/keyFigures/3/rol: Most famous convert and its leading Latin apologist
denomProfiles/marcionite/tagline: Marcion's church of the 'stranger God', with the first fixed Christian canon.
denomProfiles/marcionite/coreDoctrines/0: The God revealed by Jesus is a good 'stranger God', distinct from the just Creator of the Old Testament.
denomProfiles/marcionite/coreDoctrines/1: The Jewish Scriptures are rejected as Christian Scripture; Marcion's Antitheses set Law against Gospel.
denomProfiles/marcionite/coreDoctrines/2: A closed canon: a shortened Gospel related to Luke and ten letters of Paul (the Apostolikon).
denomProfiles/marcionite/coreDoctrines/3: Christ appeared in a body that only seemed fleshly (docetism) and was not born of Mary.
denomProfiles/marcionite/coreDoctrines/4: Salvation as rescue of souls from the Creator's world; no resurrection of the flesh.
denomProfiles/marcionite/focuses/0: Paul as the one true apostle, with the others thought to have corrupted the gospel.
denomProfiles/marcionite/focuses/1: Strict asceticism, refusing marriage and procreation in the Creator's world.
denomProfiles/marcionite/focuses/2: Organised congregations under bishops, rivalling the mainstream churches.
denomProfiles/marcionite/focuses/3: Rejection of allegorical readings that harmonised the Old Testament with the gospel.
denomProfiles/marcionite/practices/0: Baptism granted only to celibates or married couples who renounced sexual relations.
denomProfiles/marcionite/practices/1: Eucharist celebrated with bread and water rather than wine.
denomProfiles/marcionite/influenced/0/te: Many scholars argue Marcion's canon spurred the church to define its own, though how far is debated.
denomProfiles/marcionite/influenced/1/te: The largest anti-heretical work of the period defended the unity of Creator and Redeemer.
denomProfiles/marcionite/influenced/2/te: His 1921 study admired Marcion and urged Protestants to drop the Old Testament as canon.
denomProfiles/marcionite/keyFigures/0/ro: Shipowner and founder, active in Rome c. 140–160
denomProfiles/marcionite/keyFigures/2/ro: Early critic who wrote a lost treatise against Marcion
denomProfiles/marcionite/keyFigures/3/ro: Author of the five-book Against Marcion (c. 207–212)
denomProfiles/gnostic/tagline: Diverse early movements teaching salvation through saving knowledge (gnosis) of a hidden God.
denomProfiles/gnostic/coreDoctrines/0: A transcendent, unknowable God beyond the material world, from whom divine beings (aeons) emanate.
denomProfiles/gnostic/coreDoctrines/1: The visible world made by a lesser and ignorant creator, the demiurge, often identified with Israel's God.
denomProfiles/gnostic/coreDoctrines/2: Sparks of the divine trapped in some humans, awakened by knowledge brought by a revealer.
denomProfiles/gnostic/coreDoctrines/3: Christ as heavenly revealer; many groups denied that he truly suffered in the flesh.
denomProfiles/gnostic/coreDoctrines/4: Secret traditions and revelations beyond the public apostolic writings.
denomProfiles/gnostic/focuses/0: Myth and speculative cosmology, as in the Apocryphon of John.
denomProfiles/gnostic/focuses/1: Spiritual ascent of the soul past cosmic powers.
denomProfiles/gnostic/focuses/2: Reinterpretation of Genesis and of Jesus' sayings, as in the Gospel of Thomas and Gospel of Truth.
denomProfiles/gnostic/practices/0: Valentinian rites of baptism, chrism, eucharist, 'redemption' and 'bridal chamber' (Gospel of Philip).
denomProfiles/gnostic/practices/1: Study circles and schools gathered around a teacher, often inside wider churches.
denomProfiles/gnostic/practices/2: Ascetic discipline in some groups; others were accused by critics of libertinism.
denomProfiles/gnostic/practices/3: Prayers and passwords for the soul's ascent after death.
denomProfiles/gnostic/influenced/0/text: The response to Gnostic teaching helped define apostolic succession and the rule of faith.
denomProfiles/gnostic/influenced/1/text: Mani's 3rd-century religion drew on similar dualist themes.
denomProfiles/gnostic/influenced/2/text: The 1945 discovery of 13 Coptic codices transformed modern study and popular interest.
denomProfiles/gnostic/keyFigures/0/role: Alexandrian teacher in Rome c. 136–160, founder of the Valentinian school
denomProfiles/gnostic/keyFigures/2/role: Valentinian author of the Letter to Flora
denomProfiles/gnostic/keyFigures/3/role: Principal critic and source for Gnostic systems
denomProfiles/arian-homoian/tagline: Fourth-century theology of a subordinate Son, faith of the Goths and Vandals.
denomProfiles/arian-homoian/coreDoctrine: The Father alone is unbegotten and without beginning; the Son was begotten before time but 'there was when he was not' (Arius).
The Son is divine and Creator of all else, yet subordinate to and distinct in being from the Father.
Homoian formula (Rimini and Constantinople, 359–360): the Son is 'like' (homoios) the Father according to the Scriptures.
Rejection of non-scriptural terms such as ousia and the Nicene homoousios.
The Holy Spirit as a creature subordinate to the Son.
denomProfiles/arian-homoian/focuses/0: Protecting the uniqueness of the one God.
denomProfiles/arian-homoian/focuses/2: Mission among the Germanic peoples, through Ulfilas and Gothic clergy.
denomProfiles/arian-homoian/focuses/3: A church identity separating Gothic and Vandal rulers from Nicene Roman subjects.
denomProfiles/arian-homoian/practices/0: Episcopal churches with liturgy in Gothic as well as Latin and Greek.
denomProfiles/arian-homoian/practices/1: Ulfilas' Gothic Bible translation (c. 350s), surviving in the Codex Argenteus.
denomProfiles/arian-homoian/practices/2: Rebaptism of Nicene converts in Vandal North Africa.
denomProfiles/arian-homoian/practices/3: Doxologies giving glory to the Father through the Son in the Spirit.
denomProfiles/arian-homoian/influenced/0: Opposition to Arianism produced the creed of 381 and the Cappadocian doctrine of the Trinity.
denomProfiles/arian-homoian/influenced/1: Early modern anti-Trinitarians were often labelled 'Arians', though most held different views.
denomProfiles/arian-homoian/influenced/2: Their teaching that the Son is a created being is often compared to Arius.
denomProfiles/arian-homoian/keyFigures/2: Bishop and translator of the Bible into Gothic
denomProfiles/arian-homoian/keyFigures/3: Leader of the more radical Heterousian party
denomProfiles/arian-homoian/keyFigures/4: Visigothic king whose conversion at Toledo (589) ended Arianism in Spain
denomProfiles/donatist/tagline: North African church of the martyrs that refused bishops who had compromised under persecution.
denomProfiles/donatist/coreDoctrines/0: The church must be a pure body of saints, free from clergy who handed over Scriptures (traditores) in 303–305.
denomProfiles/donatist/coreDoctrines/1: Sacraments given by unworthy or schismatic clergy are invalid; converts were rebaptised, following Cyprian.
denomProfiles/donatist/coreDoctrines/2: Orthodox Nicene teaching on God and Christ; the dispute was over the church and sacraments.
denomProfiles/donatist/coreDoctrines/3: Persecution as the sign of the true church, the church of the martyrs.
denomProfiles/donatist/focuses/0: Purity and holiness of the clergy.
denomProfiles/donatist/focuses/1: Cult of the martyrs and their relics.
denomProfiles/donatist/focuses/2: Resistance to imperial interference in church affairs ('What has the emperor to do with the church?').
denomProfiles/donatist/focuses/3: Local African identity, strongest in Numidia.
denomProfiles/donatist/practices/0: Rebaptism of Catholics who joined them.
denomProfiles/donatist/practices/1: Rival bishops in almost every African town; about 270 attended the Conference of Carthage (411).
denomProfiles/donatist/practices/2: Martyr festivals and veneration at shrines.
denomProfiles/donatist/practices/3: Militant ascetic bands (circumcellions) in the countryside, sometimes violent.
denomProfiles/donatist/influenced/0/text: Against them he taught that sacraments are Christ's and valid despite an unworthy minister.
denomProfiles/donatist/influenced/1/text: His defence of imperial force against schismatics (Letter 93) shaped later Western practice.
denomProfiles/donatist/influenced/2/text: A Donatist's rules of biblical interpretation were adopted by Augustine.
denomProfiles/donatist/keyFigures/0/role: Bishop of Carthage c. 313–355 who gave the movement its name
denomProfiles/donatist/keyFigures/1/role: Successor of Donatus and leading writer
denomProfiles/donatist/keyFigures/2/role: Lay theologian of the church and of Revelation
denomProfiles/catholic/tagline: The world's largest church, in communion with the Bishop of Rome.
denomProfiles/catholic/coreDoctrines/0: One, holy, catholic and apostolic Church 'subsisting in' the Catholic Church governed by Peter's successor and the bishops (Lumen gentium 8).
denomProfiles/catholic/coreDoctrines/1: Revelation transmitted by Scripture and Tradition, authentically interpreted by the magisterium.
denomProfiles/catholic/coreDoctrines/2: Seven sacraments; in the Eucharist the bread and wine become Christ's body and blood (transubstantiation, Lateran IV 1215, Trent 1551).
denomProfiles/catholic/coreDoctrines/3: Justification by grace, received in faith and baptism, with cooperation of free will (Trent, Decree on Justification, 1547).
denomProfiles/catholic/coreDoctrines/4: Papal primacy and infallibility when defining doctrine ex cathedra (Vatican I, Pastor aeternus, 1870).
denomProfiles/catholic/coreDoctrines/5: Marian dogmas: Mother of God, perpetual virginity, Immaculate Conception (1854), Assumption (1950).
denomProfiles/catholic/focuses/0: Sacramental parish life centred on Sunday Mass.
denomProfiles/catholic/focuses/1: Education, healthcare and charity on a global scale through orders, dioceses and Caritas.
denomProfiles/catholic/focuses/2: Catholic social teaching from Rerum novarum (1891) to Laudato si' (2015).
denomProfiles/catholic/focuses/3: Evangelisation and inculturation; most Catholics now live in the global South.
denomProfiles/catholic/focuses/4: Defence of human life from conception to natural death.
denomProfiles/catholic/practices/0: Mass in the Roman Rite, in vernacular languages since the reforms after Vatican II (1969 Missal).
denomProfiles/catholic/practices/1: Confession, Lenten fasting and the liturgical year of feasts and saints.
denomProfiles/catholic/practices/2: Devotions: the rosary, eucharistic adoration, pilgrimage to Marian shrines.
denomProfiles/catholic/practices/3: Celibate priesthood in the Latin Church; religious orders such as Benedictines, Franciscans and Jesuits.
denomProfiles/catholic/practices/4: Infant baptism, with confirmation and first communion in childhood.
denomProfiles/catholic/influenced/0/text: The Reformation began as a reform movement inside the Catholic Church.
denomProfiles/catholic/influenced/1/text: The Church of England kept much Catholic order and liturgy after 1534.
denomProfiles/catholic/influenced/2/text: Eastern churches entered communion with Rome while keeping their own rites.
denomProfiles/catholic/influenced/3/text: Catholics who rejected Vatican I formed independent churches.
denomProfiles/catholic/influenced/4/text: The Catholic Charismatic Renewal began at Duquesne University in 1967.
denomProfiles/catholic/keyFigures/0/role: Apostle regarded as the first Bishop of Rome
denomProfiles/catholic/keyFigures/1/role: Pope 590–604, reformer of liturgy and mission
denomProfiles/catholic/keyFigures/2/role: Dominican theologian and Doctor of the Church
denomProfiles/catholic/keyFigures/3/role: Pope 1978–2005, global pastor and Polish dissident voice
denomProfiles/catholic/keyFigures/4/role: Pope since May 2025, the first from the United States
denomProfiles/catholic/members/note: Baptised Catholics at end of 2022, Annuarium Statisticum Ecclesiae (Vatican, 2024).
denomProfiles/catholic/inIndia: India has nearly 20 million Catholics in three churches: the Latin Church (most dioceses, rooted in the Portuguese mission at Goa from 1510 and in Tamil Nadu's coastal and Madurai missions), and the Syro-Malabar and Syro-Malankara Churches of Kerala. Tamil Nadu has large Latin Catholic communities and the national shrine of Our Lady of Good Health at Velankanni.
denomProfiles/eastern-catholic/tagline: Twenty-three Eastern churches in full communion with Rome, keeping their own rites.
denomProfiles/eastern-catholic/coreDoctr: Catholic faith in full: the seven sacraments, the ecumenical councils and the primacy and infallibility of the Pope (Vatican I, 1870).
Each church is sui iuris (self-governing) with its own hierarchy, liturgy, spirituality and law.
Eastern traditions are equal in dignity to the Latin rite (Vatican II, Orientalium Ecclesiarum, 1964).
Eastern theological emphases such as theosis may be expressed alongside Latin formulations.
Canon law in the Code of Canons of the Eastern Churches (1990).
denomProfiles/eastern-catholic/focuses/0: Preserving Byzantine, Alexandrian, Antiochene, Armenian and East Syriac liturgical heritage.
denomProfiles/eastern-catholic/focuses/1: Unity with Rome without Latinisation, and recovery of traditions lost in earlier centuries.
denomProfiles/eastern-catholic/focuses/2: Survival of minority communities in the Middle East and Eastern Europe.
denomProfiles/eastern-catholic/focuses/3: Diaspora churches in the Americas, Europe and Australia.
denomProfiles/eastern-catholic/focuses/4: A bridge, sometimes contested, in Catholic–Orthodox relations.
denomProfiles/eastern-catholic/practices: Eastern liturgies such as the Divine Liturgy of St John Chrysostom or the Qurbana of Addai and Mari.
Baptism, chrismation and communion given together to infants in most churches.
Married priests ordained in the homelands of most churches.
Patriarchs and major archbishops elected by their synods, confirmed by or in communion with the Pope.
Icons, Eastern fasts and calendars, and the Jesus Prayer in Byzantine churches.
denomProfiles/eastern-catholic/influence: The Balamand Statement (1993) rejected 'uniatism' as a method of union while affirming these churches' right to exist.
Eastern bishops such as Maximos IV Sayegh pressed the council on collegiality and the vernacular.
The largest Eastern Catholic church in Asia.
denomProfiles/eastern-catholic/keyFigure: Metropolitan of Lviv 1901–44 and champion of Eastern identity
Melkite Patriarch and voice of the East at Vatican II
Ukrainian Major Archbishop imprisoned in the Soviet Gulag 1945–63
denomProfiles/eastern-catholic/members/n: Approximate total of the 23 churches in CNEWA, The Eastern Catholic Churches 2017.
denomProfiles/eastern-catholic/inIndia: India has two Eastern Catholic churches, both Kerala-based St Thomas Christian bodies: the Syro-Malabar (East Syriac rite) and the Syro-Malankara (West Syriac rite), with eparchies across India including Tamil Nadu.
